explanation.value: Treat each file as a stream that can deliver its next fixed-size block (64 bytes) regardless of how the input was chunked. Group files by total size first. Then repeatedly refine each candidate group: read the next block from every member and split the group by block content. Groups that shrink to one file are dropped and never read again; a group whose members have all been read to the end is a duplicate group. This is the same partition-refinement idea used by real duplicate finders, which read files in pieces rather than all at once.
